title: Normalized compact-support comparisons on finite rational inputs
statement: Fix the same relative finite-type geometry, coefficient construction P and compactification c as in StageAction, a NativeGeometry for l, and a specified StageAction. There exist realizations of X, Y and c.Z and coefficient changes from each completed finite integral coefficient ring to the native ring, whose values equal the chosen realization coefficient maps at those three schemes. For each finite unlifted coefficient field E there is a natural isomorphism between the two compact-support realizations restricted to the E-stage inclusion. These stagewise isomorphisms respect every source isoToStage, including identity stages. The normalization certificate says that every common-stage natural isomorphism whose components are these finite-stage components satisfies the unchanged IntegralNormalization predicate, namely the original six-arrow scalar-mate equation on integral finite-Tor inputs. This assertion does not assert descent on arbitrary common-field Hom classes or preservation for arbitrary native constructible objects.

proof.text: Use the constructible realization theorem at X, Y and c.Z. The proper factor makes c.Z finite type over the same algebraic closure; the characteristic follows from the cardinality of D.k0. Apply the normalized coefficient-change lemma separately at each finite unlifted E. Its equality for every presentation gives all three change_source, change_target and change_middle fields.

proof.text: The coefficient prime is a unit in global functions by the finite-field datum. Map it through germs to every residue field of X. Apply the proved integral-localization bridge to the chosen source/target realizations and coefficient maps. It supplies a rational natural isomorphism alpha_E at every finite stage and its original six-arrow component normalization.

proof.text: For any common-stage gamma with the prescribed finite-stage components, evaluate its component hypothesis at the inclusion of the integral representative K. Equality of these same-typed arrows transports IntegralComponent for the normalized finite-stage component to gamma. IntegralComponent is the original IntegralNormalization formula with the component made a parameter, so this proves the unchanged integral certificate. Assemble CoefficientFamily and FiniteComparison.
